artifacts.title: Huffman v. Tennessee Valley Presbytery
artifacts.synopsis: TE Huffman filed an appeal after the 50th GA amended BCO 38-1 to change the remedy from complaint to appeal, but his case originated and was nearly complete under the prior rule allowing complaint. The SJC found the case judicially out of order and remanded to Tennessee Valley Presbytery to adjudicate as a complaint under the then-existing rule, resetting the clock for presbytery action.

artifacts.synopsis: Seven members of a PCA mission church were tried and censured by a provisional Session for opposing the organizing minister's continuation as permanent pastor. The SJC sustained the appeal and reversed the convictions, holding that the indictments lacked required specificity under BCO 32-5, that the accused had no sinned against the fifth or ninth commandment by expressing opinions about ministerial suitability, and that the right to choose a pastor belongs to the congregation—not the provisional Session. A concurring opinion addressed indictment requirements, standard of review in appeals, and congregational rights in mission church minister selection.

artifacts.synopsis: RE Dudt was convicted and suspended from office by the Midway Presbyterian Church Session for emailing the congregation an SJC decision and expressing disagreement with a Session action, which the Session characterized as violating his ordination vows. The SJC sustained the appeal, reversing in whole and rendering a verdict of not guilty, finding that the Session had no constitutional authority to forbid Dudt from distributing the SJC decision and that the charges of false statements were not proven. A concurring opinion by several judges cautioned against elders emailing congregations in disagreement with Session decisions.

artifacts.title: Crouse v. Northwest Georgia Presbytery
artifacts.synopsis: The SJC sustained the complaint, ruling that a Session erred by prescreening and eliminating a deacon's nomination for ruling elder before the mandatory instruction and examination process required by BCO 24-1. The decision held that BCO 24-1's language is mandatory and that sessions cannot add a preliminary vetting step that bypasses the required sequence of instruction and examination.

artifacts.synopsis: RE Gerald Hedman complained that Pacific Northwest Presbytery unconstitutionally adopted five not-guilty verdicts regarding TE Peter Leithart's teachings on baptism, covenants, imputation, justification, and union with Christ. The SJC denied the complaint, finding it was bound by the Record of the Case and that Complainant had not demonstrated clear error on the part of Presbytery, with concurring and dissenting opinions discussing the scope of review, standing, and concerns about Leithart's sacramental theology.

artifacts.synopsis: Matt Ruff complained that Nashville Presbytery failed to conduct an adequate BCO 31-2 investigation and to find a strong presumption of guilt against TE George Grant; the SJC sustained both complaints and remanded, finding the investigation record was incomplete and internally inconsistent, and that conduct described by the Presbytery's own Shepherding Committee as 'sin' required an explanation as to why no strong presumption of guilt existed.

artifacts.synopsis: The Standing Judicial Commission sustained an appeal by E. L. Fitzsimmons against Evangel Presbytery's handling of his appeal from excommunication. The court found that Presbytery erred by failing to notify the appellant of the time, date, and place for hearing the appeal and by rescinding its earlier finding that the appeal was in order, thus failing to adjudicate the appeal properly. The case was remanded to Evangel Presbytery for proper adjudication on the merits.

artifacts.title: Nickoley v. Rocky Mountain
artifacts.synopsis: The SJC found that Rocky Mountain Presbytery erred in immediately deposing Rev. Bruce Nickoley from ministry on a contumacy charge without providing him due process rights and a full trial. The case was remanded for either proper trial or revocation of the deposition judgment.
